### Per-asset notes

**C03 — Ninh Binh (100 MW).** Scheduled for retirement by 2030 under Revised PDP8 if the plant cannot adopt new technology or meet emission standards.
The two coal-fired power plants set to cease operation by 2030 are the 440 MW Pha Lai and 100 MW Ninh Binh.

**C01 — Pha Lai 1 (440 MW).** Same retirement condition as Ninh Binh above. Soviet-era subcritical units, oldest major coal plant still operating.

**C33 — Thai Binh 2 (1,200 MW).** Long-delayed PVN project. Report 32 and 58 both assessed multi-year delay.
The long-delayed Thai Binh 2 Thermal Power Plant was officially inaugurated on April 27

2023.

**C40 — Long Phu 1 (1,200 MW).** Construction reached ~78% before halting due to US sanctions on Russian EPC contractor (Power Machines). Study E542 noted the plant was "tạm ngừng" (suspended). Still listed under construction in PDP8 Table 2 but completion date highly uncertain.

**C41–C45 — Shelved coal projects.** PDP8 Table 3 lists these five projects as facing difficulties with investor changes and financing. The Decision gave a deadline of June 2024 for Cong Thanh; the province subsequently proposed conversion to LNG. Nam Dinh 1, Quang Tri, Vinh Tan 3, and Song Hau 2 have lost their BOT investors' commitment and face no realistic path to financial close as coal plants.

**C54 — Kien Luong (3,600 MW).** Investment license revoked by Prime Minister. Per study E542: "Thủ tướng đã thu hồi giấy phép đầu tư."

**C56 — Uong Bi original (105 MW).**
As of January 2025, the total capacity of the station was listed as 630 MW

, confirming the original 105 MW units have been retired.

**C57 — Formosa Ha Tinh Phase 1.** Complex multi-unit captive power station for Formosa steel. PDP7A Table 1 lists coal-fired units (#2, #5 at 150 MW each) and blast-furnace gas units (#3, #4 at 100 MW each) entering service in 2016. The 2010–11 EVN AR already showed 150 MW. Total Phase 1 estimated ~550 MW from mixed coal and BFG. Exact operating capacity needs operator disclosure. Confidence MEDIUM.

**G11 — O Mon 1 (660 MW).** Designed as CCGT but initially running on oil/DO pending Lo B gas pipeline. PDP8 Table 5 lists it for conversion to Lo B gas. EVN AR 2017 and 2018 classify it under "oil-fired" at 660 MW. Two-unit plant: 2×330 MW open-cycle turbines now; conversion to combined cycle upon gas availability.

**G14–G16 — O Mon II/III/IV.** All three depend on Lo B offshore gas field development (Block B – O Mon pipeline). Report 32 noted O Mon III delayed 5 years, O Mon IV delayed 3 years from PDP7A schedule. The Lo B gas project has faced repeated delays since 2010s.

**G17–G21 — Dung Quat and Mien Trung gas plants.** All depend on Ca Voi Xanh (Blue Whale) offshore gas field operated by ExxonMobil. Report 32 noted these projects are "đồng bộ khí CVX" (synchronized to CVX gas schedule). PDP8 Table 5 maintains all five projects.

**G23 — Kien Giang I & II (1,500 MW).** Originally in PDP7A for Lo B gas. Reports 32 and 58 both assessed "sau 2030" and "khó đáp ứng do vấn đề nhiên liệu" (hard to meet due to fuel issues). Dropped from PDP8 Table 5. Status: Cancelled.

**L01–L02 — Nhon Trach 3 & 4 (1,624 MW total).**
Vietnam's first LNG-to-power projects. The PM attended the inauguration ceremony on December 14

2025. Each unit rated at 812 MW CCGT.

**L03 — LNG Hai Phong Phase I (1,600 MW).** Added to national plan under Revised PDP8 (Decision 768, April 2025).
Haiphong LNG power station is under construction.
The investor consortium includes Tokyo Gas, Kyuden International, and Truong Thanh Group JSC.

Construction start targeted September 2025.

**L07 — LNG Hiep Phuoc Phase I (1,200 MW).**
EVN and Hiep Phuoc Power Company Limited signed a PPA for the plant.

**L15 — LNG Bac Lieu (3,200 MW).** Delta Offshore Energy proposed project using floating storage regasification unit (FSRU). Has faced repeated delays and skepticism about viability. Listed in PDP8 at 3,200 MW but status remains uncertain.
